advances: An intrinsic mixed-volume extraction maximizer and scalar continuous dilation with affine base shear and translation. The stress has arbitrarily small total slack.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
A convex combination of positive-fiber bases with integer barycenter has a positive $q$-fiber, because its Minkowski combination contains a translate of one positively scaled $q$-fiber. Thus $P_D$ is lattice-convex, and the hull of the lifted positive fibers has exactly those fibers by convexity of $D$. The map $(z,x)\mapsto(z,b+B(z-j)+s(x-c))$ is a lattice-preserving affine bijection, carrying this hull into $C$ under the fit. If its base span is full, its integral centroid base $j$ is interior to the base projection of $C$, forcing $q=d$ as in the intrinsic variable-shape attainment theorem. The transformed positive hull is then ambient-full. Otherwise use that theorem's one-sided thickening inside $C$ to retain its exact integer trace. The realized measure is $s^q$ times the pushforward of the original, since each measured fiber scales by $s^q$ in its $q$-space. Hence its centroid is $(j,b)$, and the affine bijection of containing closed halfspaces preserves normalized depth. This gives feasibility, and maximality yields $s\le1$.

Restrict the base coordinates of $B$ to the $k$-dimensional span of $P_D-j$. Set $\eta=s-1$, $b_0=b-c$. Each fit is equivalent to the family of linear inequalities
$
\eta\,u\cdot(x-c)+u\cdot B(z-j)+u\cdot b_0
\le h_{C_z}(u)-u\cdot x
\quad(z\in P_D,\ x\in D_z,\ \|u\|=1).
$
The effective parameter dimension is $p=1+dk+d$. Zero is feasible and no feasible point has $\eta>0$ because then $s>1$. A finite initial subfamily makes the feasible region bounded: constrain the coordinate images of two distinct points at one positive fiber and one point at each of $k+1$ affinely independent sites, with normals $\pm e_l$. Such points exist since $q>0$. The linear evaluation map in $(\eta,B,b_0)$ is injective, since subtracting the two images at the same site first determines $\eta$, and the affinely independent sites then determine the affine base term. All image coordinates are bounded by the target support values, so the parameter set is bounded and closed.

Intersect this compact region with $\eta\ge\epsilon$. Its intersection with the full family is empty, hence finitely many more inequalities already exclude it. The resulting finite feasible bounded LP has optimal value in $[0,\epsilon)$. Duality gives nonnegative multipliers summing the gradients to the objective gradient and summing the slacks to that optimum. Conic Carathéodory applied to the gradient-plus-slack vectors in $\mathbb R^{p+1}$ reduces the number to at most $p+1=d(k+1)+2$. The resulting equations are those in the statement. The effective base equations give the ambient equations because every $z_i-j$ lies in the chosen span.
statement:
Use the intrinsic variable-shape extraction problem with ambient source $C$, $q=\dim_H(C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d))>0$, and fixed threshold $\beta$. Let $D$ maximize its positive intrinsic retained mass $m$, with true centroid $(j,c)$, and let $P_D=\{z:\mathcal H^q(D_z)>0\}$ have affine dimension $k$. Suppose $s>0$ and
$
b+B(z-j)+s(D_z-c)\subseteq C_z\quad (z\in P_D)
$
for a continuous vector $b$ and linear base-to-continuous map $B$. These positive transformed fibers are realizable by an ambient extraction in $C$ with mass $s^q m$, centroid $(j,b)$ and the same normalized depth there. In particular $s\le1$. For every $\epsilon>0$ there exist at most $d(k+1)+2$ triples $((z_i,x_i),u_i,\lambda_i)$ with $z_i\in P_D,x_i\in D_{z_i},\|u_i\|=1,\lambda_i\ge0$, satisfying
$
\sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0,\qquad
\sum_i\lambda_i u_i(z_i-j)^{\mathsf T}=0,\qquad
\sum_i\lambda_i u_i\cdot(x_i-c)=1,\qquad
0\le\sum_i\lambda_i[h_{C_{z_i}}(u_i)-u_i\cdot x_i]<\epsilon .
$
title: Depth-preserving affine fits and approximate extraction contact stresses
